answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when it misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Honest agents that wander through many transactions build a public history, and the network treats long-lived, well-behaved identities as a beacon of trust: new agents start with low limits and earn higher throughput only through sustained good conduct. Like a tide, reputation rises slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so every fake identity costs the attacker real capital and time.
